trigger: I am being searched in a degrading way
description: What to do if a search on your body is humiliating, or a woman is searched by a male officer.

steps.text: You have a right to dignity; no one may treat you in a degrading or inhuman way (s.34(1)).
Ask to be searched in a private place and, for a woman, by a female officer.
Say clearly and calmly: 'This search is degrading. I ask to be treated with dignity (s.34).'
You must not be singled out or mistreated because of your sex, tribe, religion, or status (s.42).
Do not physically resist, but do not consent to being stripped or humiliated in public.
Note who conducted the search, where, and any witnesses present.
Call your lawyer or a trusted person and report to the NHRC afterwards.
